name: lcm

subject.description:
Write a function who takes two unsigned int as parameters and returns the
computed LCM of those parameters.

LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) of two non-zero integers is the smallest postive
integer divisible by the both integers.

A LCM can be calculated in two ways:

- You can calculate every multiples of each integers until you have a common
multiple other than 0

- You can use the HCF (Highest Common Factor) of these two integers and
calculate as follows:

    LCM(x, y) = | x * y | / HCF(x, y)

 | x * y | means "Absolute value of the product of x by y"

If at least one integer is null, LCM is equal to 0.

Your function must be prototyped as follows:

 unsigned int    lcm(unsigned int a, unsigned int b);

name: brainfuck

subject.description:
Write a Brainfuck interpreter program. The source code will be given as first parameter. The code will always be valid, with no more than 4096 operations.

Brainfuck is a minimalist language. It consists of an array of bytes (2048 bytes) initialized to zero, and a pointer to its first byte.

Every operator consists of a single character:
- '>' increment the pointer
- '<' decrement the pointer
- '+' increment the pointed byte
- '-' decrement the pointed byte
- '.' print the pointed byte on standard output
- '[' go to the matching ']' if the pointed byte is 0 (while start)
- ']' go to the matching '[' if the pointed byte is not 0 (while end)

Any other character is a comment.

For example, base 4 would be "0123" and base 16 "0123456789ABCDEF".

subject.description:
Write a program that takes rows of a chessboard as arguments and checks if the King is in a check position.

Only Pawns (P), Bishops (B), Rooks (R) and a Queen (Q) play against a single King (K). All other characters are empty squares.

Pawn threatens the square diagonally in front of it (one row toward the King's row, i.e. at row+1 relative to the pawn, both columns adjacent). Bishop threatens along diagonals. Rook threatens along its row/column. Queen threatens along both. A piece can only capture the first piece it finds along its line of sight — any piece in between blocks it, even if that piece isn't the one giving check.

If the King is in check, print 'Success' followed by a newline, otherwise print 'Fail' followed by a newline. With no arguments, print only a newline.

With no arguments, print only a newline.

name: rpn_calc

subject.description:
Write a program that takes a string containing an equation written in Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) as its first argument, evaluates it, and prints the result followed by a newline.

In RPN, every operator follows its operands; each operator evaluates the previous 2 operands and the result replaces them for the next operator. Operands and operators must be separated by at least one space. Implement +, -, *, /, and %.

If the string isn't valid or there isn't exactly one argument, print 'Error' followed by a newline. All operands fit in an int.

name: options

subject.description:
Write a program that takes an undefined number of arguments treated as options and writes on standard output a representation of those options as groups of bytes followed by a newline.

An option is an argument that begins with '-' followed by one or more characters from a-z. All options are stored in a single int, one bit per letter (a=bit0 ... z=bit25).

Running without arguments, or with '-h' present, prints the usage line. An invalid option prints 'Invalid Option' followed by a newline.

name: biggest_pal

subject.description:
Write a program named biggest_pal that takes a string as argument and prints the biggest palindrome contained inside this string, followed by a newline.

The string contains only lowercase characters.

If there are two palindromes of the same length, print the last one.

If there is more or less than 1 argument, the program prints only a newline.
